content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: In-Context Learning and Zero-Shot/Few-Shot Prompting in NLP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized Natural Language Processing by demonstrating the ability to perform tasks without requiring explicit gradient updates or fine-tuning. This paradigm shift relies heavily on In-Context Learning (ICL) and strategic prompting techniques, specifically zero-shot and few-shot prompting."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding In-Context Learning (ICL)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In-Context Learning refers to the ability of a frozen language model to learn a task purely from the examples provided within the prompt during inference time. Unlike traditional supervised learning, model parameters are not updated via backpropagation. Instead, the model leverages its pre-existing representations and pattern-matching capabilities acquired during pre-training to infer the underlying mapping function."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Zero-Shot Prompting"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"In zero-shot prompting, the model is given a task description and an input without any prior examples of the desired output. The model relies entirely on its generalized knowledge base to generate the correct response."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"prompt = \"Classify the sentiment of the following review as positive, neutral, or negative.\\nReview: The battery life on this device is exceptionally poor.\\nSentiment:\""},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Few-Shot Prompting"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Few-shot prompting extends zero-shot prompting by providing a small number of demonstrations (input-output pairs) within the prompt context. This approach helps the model understand the exact format, style, and reasoning required for the target task."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"prompt = \"Convert product descriptions into JSON format.\\n\\nDescription: Apple iPhone 13, 128GB, Blue, 799 USD\\nJSON: {\\\"item\\\": \\\"iPhone 13\\\", \\\"brand\\\": \\\"Apple\\\", \\\"storage\\\": \\\"128GB\\\", \\\"color\\\": \\\"Blue\\\", \\\"price\\\": \\\"799 USD\\\"}\\n\\nDescription: Samsung Galaxy S22, 256GB, Phantom Black, 849 USD\\nJSON: {\\\"item\\\": \\\"Galaxy S22\\\", \\\"brand\\\": \\\"Samsung\\\", \\\"storage\\\": \\\"256GB\\\", \\\"color\\\": \\\"Phantom Black\\\", \\\"price\\\": \\\"849 USD\\\"}\\n\\nDescription: Google Pixel 7, 128GB, Lemongrass, 599 USD\\nJSON:\""},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Key Best Practices for Implementation"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Task Definition: Clearly state the objective at the beginning of the prompt before supplying any examples."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Formatting Consistency: Ensure that all few-shot examples follow an identical structural layout to prevent confusing the model."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Token Budget Management: Keep track of context window limitations, as adding too many few-shot examples can exceed the maximum token limit."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Label Space Design: Use distinct, unambiguous labels, especially when performing classification tasks."}]
